source_evidence.anchor: Section 2.1, LR factor representation and Frobenius norm convention
source_evidence.observation: At this anchor, an LR approximation is represented as A_tilde = XY^T with X having orthonormal columns. The unsubscripted norm is defined to be the Frobenius norm, and the analysis is explicitly normwise. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953; anchor: LR representation and Frobenius norm convention]

source_evidence.anchor: Continuation of the Frobenius norm properties
source_evidence.observation: The Frobenius norm is submultiplicative, invariant under multiplication by a matrix with orthonormal columns, and satisfies the blockwise-to-global identity. Orthonormal columns require X^T X = I but not XX^T = I. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: continuation of Frobenius norm properties]

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (2.5) and the definition of gamma_k
source_evidence.observation: The arithmetic model is fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1+delta), |delta| <= u, for op in {+, -, multiplication, division}. The paper defines gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) when ku < 1 and permits non-integer gamma indices. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.5) and gamma_k definition]

For a conventional matrix product with inner dimension b, the computed product satisfies C_hat = AB + Delta C and ||Delta C|| <= gamma_b ||A|| ||B||. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: Lemma 2.1, equation (2.7)]

The analysis assumes LR approximations satisfy normwise truncation bounds while rounding in their truncated-SVD construction is ignored. It also assumes throughout that unit roundoff u is safely smaller than the LR threshold epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: Assumption 2.1 and following paragraph]

Lemma 3.2 supplies the cross-referenced forward-error bound for multiplying an LR matrix by a full matrix, with constant b+r^(3/2). [PDF p. 7, printed p. 957; anchor: Lemma 3.2, equations (3.5)-(3.6)]

source_evidence.anchor: Paragraph beginning 'It is important to note that Lemma 3.1'
source_evidence.observation: The paper states that its results provide normwise, rather than componentwise, error bounds because LR approximations do not provide useful componentwise bounds. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 958; anchor: paragraph on normwise error bounds]

Lemma 3.3 specifies real b-by-b matrices A and B, shared-rank factors A_tilde = X_A Y_A^T and B_tilde = Y_B X_B^T, orthonormal columns in X_A and X_B, two truncation bounds, two permitted evaluation orders, and the two stated forward-error bounds with c = b+2r^(3/2). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 and equations (3.10)-(3.11)]

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Lemma 3.3, first intermediate product
source_evidence.observation: For the first parenthesization, the proof applies Lemma 3.2 to W = A_tilde Y_B and obtains ||Delta W|| <= gamma_(b+r^(3/2)) ||A_tilde|| ||B_tilde||. The second parenthesization is declared analogous. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: proof of Lemma 3.3, first intermediate product]

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Lemma 3.3, final multiplication and replacement by A+E_A and B+E_B
source_evidence.observation: The final multiplication by X_B^T is bounded, the accumulated floating-point error F is reduced to gamma_c ||A_tilde|| ||B_tilde||, and replacing A_tilde and B_tilde by A+E_A and B+E_B yields equation (3.11), including all epsilon and gamma_c cross terms. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: proof completion of Lemma 3.3]

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (3.12) and transition to intermediate recompression
source_evidence.observation: Immediately after Lemma 3.3, the paper gives the specialization beta_A = ||A|| and beta_B = ||B||, then introduces intermediate recompression as a separate algorithm covered by Lemma 3.4 rather than Lemma 3.3. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: equation (3.12) and recompression transition]

binders: Explicitly, A and B are real b-by-b matrices, A_tilde = X_A Y_A^T, and B_tilde = Y_B X_B^T. The displayed dimensions make X_A, Y_A, Y_B, and X_B b-by-r matrices. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 factor display]
The two approximations use the same rank parameter r and the same LR threshold epsilon, with scaling parameters beta_A and beta_B. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 hypotheses]
C denotes the exact LR product A_tilde B_tilde, while C_hat denotes the result produced in floating-point arithmetic. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 computation clause]
The roundoff parameter is u, gamma_k = ku/(1-ku), and the lemma sets c = b+2r^(3/2). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: gamma_k definition] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.10)]
hypotheses: X_A and X_B have orthonormal columns, equivalently X_A^T X_A = I_r and X_B^T X_B = I_r; no orthonormality condition is imposed on Y_A or Y_B. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 orthonormality clause]
The exact approximations satisfy ||A-A_tilde|| <= epsilon beta_A and ||B-B_tilde|| <= epsilon beta_B. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 approximation inequalities]

The product is evaluated using either (X_A(Y_A^T Y_B))X_B^T or X_A((Y_A^T Y_B)X_B^T), with the parentheses fixing the intermediate-product order. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 computation clause]
The standard floating-point model (2.5) and conventional matrix-product bound (2.7) are inherited by the computation. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.5) and Lemma 2.1 equation (2.7)]

Because gamma_k is defined only for ku < 1, use of gamma_c inherits the condition cu < 1 for c = b+2r^(3/2). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: gamma_k definition] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: definition of c]
The paper's standing analysis assumption is that u is safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: paragraph following Assumption 2.1]
conclusions: For either permitted evaluation order, ||C_hat-A_tilde B_tilde|| <= gamma_c ||A_tilde|| ||B_tilde||, where c = b+2r^(3/2). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.10)]
Consequently, ||C_hat-AB|| <= gamma_c ||A|| ||B|| + epsilon(1+gamma_c)(beta_A||B|| + ||A||beta_B + epsilon beta_A beta_B). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.11)]
definitions_and_conventions: Every unsubscripted matrix norm in the result is the Frobenius norm, not the spectral norm or a componentwise measure. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953; anchor: Frobenius norm convention]
A matrix with orthonormal columns satisfies X^T X = I; it need not be square or satisfy XX^T = I. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: continuation of Frobenius norm properties]

The general LR-threshold setup treats epsilon as positive and uses positive beta scaling parameters; Lemma 3.3 itself states only the resulting approximation inequalities. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: Assumption 2.1] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 hypotheses]

The immediately following specialization beta_A = ||A|| and beta_B = ||B|| gives ||C_hat-AB|| <= (2epsilon+epsilon^2+gamma_c(1+epsilon)^2)||A||||B||; this is equation (3.12), not an additional hypothesis of Lemma 3.3. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: equation (3.12)]
implicit_context: The displayed matrix dimensions and orthonormal-column requirements imply positive integer matrix dimensions and r <= b, although Lemma 3.3 does not explicitly quantify b and r or state this inequality. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 factor display]

The paper assumes accurate truncated-SVD construction of LR approximations in its BLR setting, but Lemma 3.3 is stated conditionally from the two norm inequalities and does not require a specific construction algorithm in its own text. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: Assumption 2.1] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 hypotheses]
No symmetry, definiteness, nonsingularity, or invertibility condition is imposed on A or B in Lemma 3.3. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: opening of Lemma 3.3]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Lemma 3.3 concerns direct multiplication of two LR factors with the middle product Y_A^T Y_B formed first and with either left-associated or right-associated completion. The proof treats (X_A(Y_A^T Y_B))X_B^T and says the other order is analogous. Intermediate recompression of Y_A^T Y_B is introduced only afterward and belongs to Lemma 3.4, so it is outside this contract. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 computation clause and proof] [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: transition to Lemma 3.4]
numerical_model: Scalar operations obey fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1+delta), |delta| <= u, for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.5)]

gamma_k is exactly ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1; the paper explicitly permits non-integer gamma indices, which is necessary for indices containing r^(3/2). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: gamma_k definition]
The inherited matrix-product model is C_hat = AB+Delta C with ||Delta C|| <= gamma_b||A||||B|| when b is the inner dimension. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.7)]

For the first evaluation order, the proof first obtains ||Delta W|| <= gamma_(b+r^(3/2))||A_tilde||||B_tilde|| and then bounds the final multiplication by gamma_(r^(3/2))(1+gamma_(b+r^(3/2)))||A_tilde||||B_tilde|| before combining these contributions into gamma_c. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: proof's W_hat bound] [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: proof's final multiplication bound]

Rounding in the construction of LR approximations is ignored under the paper's standing truncated-SVD assumption, and u is assumed safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: Assumption 2.1 and following paragraph]
error_notions: Equation (3.10) is a normwise forward-error bound from the computed C_hat to the exact product of the supplied LR approximations, A_tilde B_tilde. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.10)]

Equation (3.11) is a normwise forward-error bound from C_hat to the exact full-matrix product AB; it combines floating-point product error with the two LR approximation errors. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.11)]
Neither equation is stated as a backward-error result for the LR-by-LR product. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 conclusions]
The paper explicitly characterizes its LR results as normwise and does not claim useful componentwise bounds. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 958; anchor: paragraph on normwise error bounds]
norms: The norm is ||M||_F = (sum_(i,j)|m_ij|^2)^(1/2), written without a subscript throughout the paper. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953; anchor: Frobenius norm definition]

The proof relies on Frobenius submultiplicativity, ||AB|| <= ||A||||B||, and invariance under orthonormal factors. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953; anchor: Frobenius norm properties] [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: continuation of those properties]

The orthonormal outer factors yield the identities used in the proof, including ||Y_B|| = ||B_tilde|| and ||X_B|| = sqrt(r). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: proof's W_hat bound] [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: proof's final multiplication bound]
constants_and_indexing: The final constant is exactly c = b+2r^(3/2), and the roundoff coefficient is gamma_c rather than gamma_b or an unspecified constant. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.10)]
Both LR factorizations use the same displayed rank r: X_A and Y_B are b-by-r, while Y_A^T and X_B^T are r-by-b. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 factor dimensions]

The proof's intermediate gamma indices are b+r^(3/2) and r^(3/2), which combine using the paper's gamma identities into b+2r^(3/2). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: gamma identities] [PDF pp. 9-10, printed pp. 959-960; anchor: proof of Lemma 3.3]
higher_order_terms: Equations (3.10) and (3.11) contain no big-O remainder; their displayed terms are explicit. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equations (3.10)-(3.11)]

The epsilon beta_A beta_B term inside the parentheses in equation (3.11) must be retained; after the outer epsilon is applied, it contributes epsilon^2(1+gamma_c)beta_A beta_B. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.11)]

The factor (1+gamma_c) multiplying all three truncation contributions must be retained, including the mixed roundoff-truncation terms. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: F and G decomposition yielding equation (3.11)]
exceptional_values: The selected passages do not separately discuss overflow, underflow, subnormal numbers, NaNs, infinities, or division by zero; they state only the standard relative-error model (2.5). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.5)]

The only explicit domain restriction attached to gamma_k is ku < 1, hence gamma_c requires cu < 1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: gamma_k definition] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: c definition]

undebatable_constraints: A and B must be real b-by-b matrices with supplied rank-r factorizations A_tilde = X_A Y_A^T and B_tilde = Y_B X_B^T. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: opening and factor display of Lemma 3.3]
Only X_A and X_B are required to have orthonormal columns. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: orthonormality clause of Lemma 3.3]
Both approximation bounds, ||A-A_tilde|| <= epsilon beta_A and ||B-B_tilde|| <= epsilon beta_B, are required. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: approximation inequalities]
The theorem covers both stated parenthesizations and uses the same bound for each. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: computation clause preceding equation (3.10)]
The first conclusion compares C_hat with A_tilde B_tilde and has right-hand side gamma_c||A_tilde||||B_tilde||. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.10)]
The second conclusion compares C_hat with AB and includes gamma_c||A||||B|| plus epsilon(1+gamma_c)(beta_A||B||+||A||beta_B+epsilon beta_A beta_B). [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.11)]
All norms are Frobenius norms and the claims are normwise. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953; anchor: Frobenius norm convention] [PDF p. 8, printed p. 958; anchor: normwise-error paragraph]
The constant is c = b+2r^(3/2), with gamma_c defined by gamma_k = ku/(1-ku). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: gamma_k definition] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equation (3.10)]
Intermediate recompression is not part of Lemma 3.3. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: transition from equation (3.12) to Lemma 3.4]

ambiguities.issue: Lemma 3.3 does not explicitly quantify b and r or state 1 <= r <= b. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 factor display]
ambiguities.evidence: The source gives only the matrix dimensions b-by-r and the requirement that X_A and X_B have orthonormal columns, from which positive integer dimensions and r <= b are inferred. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: factor dimensions and orthonormality clause]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization may make the dimension and rank constraints explicit, but it should identify them as type-level or inferred conditions rather than additional written hypotheses.

ambiguities.issue: The signs and intended choices of beta_A and beta_B are not restated inside Lemma 3.3. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: approximation inequalities]
ambiguities.evidence: The earlier LR setup uses positive beta parameters and local or global norm scales, while Lemma 3.3 only assumes the two inequalities; the following equation (3.12) separately treats beta_A=||A|| and beta_B=||B||. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: Assumption 2.1] [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: equation (3.12)]
ambiguities.impact: The general contract must not replace beta_A and beta_B by matrix norms unless explicitly specializing to equation (3.12).

ambiguities.issue: The standing condition that u is 'safely smaller' than epsilon is qualitative. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: paragraph following Assumption 2.1]
ambiguities.evidence: No numerical factor or exact inequality stronger than the gamma-domain condition is supplied for the phrase 'safely smaller.' [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: paragraph following Assumption 2.1]
ambiguities.impact: A faithful formal statement should either retain this qualitative standing assumption separately or use only explicit conditions such as cu < 1; it should not invent a numerical threshold.

ambiguities.issue: The source fixes matrix-level parenthesization but not a loop-level summation order or named matrix-multiplication implementation. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 computation clause]
ambiguities.evidence: The proof invokes the generic product bound (2.7) and Lemma 3.2 rather than specifying an implementation beyond the two parenthesizations. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.7)] [PDF pp. 9-10, printed pp. 959-960; anchor: proof of Lemma 3.3]
ambiguities.impact: The computation should be modeled through the stated local error bounds, not through an unstated concrete loop order.

ambiguities.issue: The selected passage contains no explicit exceptional-value policy. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.5)]
ambiguities.evidence: Overflow, underflow, subnormals, NaNs, and infinities are not mentioned alongside the standard relative-error model. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.5)]
ambiguities.impact: Such exclusions may be conventional consequences of adopting the model, but they must not be presented as separately stated paper hypotheses.

ambiguities.issue: The provenance of A_tilde and B_tilde is not fixed by Lemma 3.3 itself. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 hypotheses]
ambiguities.evidence: The broader paper assumes truncated-SVD LR approximations, but Lemma 3.3 only consumes factor forms, orthonormality, and normwise approximation bounds. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955; anchor: Assumption 2.1] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3]
ambiguities.impact: A faithful theorem may abstract over any approximations satisfying the stated conditions and should not require a particular SVD algorithm unless importing the broader BLR construction context.

contract_plain_english: Given real b-by-b matrices A and B and shared-rank LR approximations A_tilde=X_A Y_A^T and B_tilde=Y_B X_B^T, with only X_A and X_B required to have orthonormal columns and with Frobenius-norm errors at most epsilon beta_A and epsilon beta_B, respectively, compute A_tilde B_tilde in either of the two parenthesized orders stated by Lemma 3.3. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: Lemma 3.3 hypotheses and computation clause] Under the paper's standard floating-point model, the computed C_hat differs from the exact LR product by at most gamma_c||A_tilde||||B_tilde||, where c=b+2r^(3/2), and differs from the exact full product AB by at most gamma_c||A||||B||+epsilon(1+gamma_c)(beta_A||B||+||A||beta_B+epsilon beta_A beta_B). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954; anchor: equation (2.5) and gamma_k definition] [PDF p. 9, printed p. 959; anchor: equations (3.10)-(3.11)] These are explicit normwise forward-error bounds with no omitted big-O term, and they do not cover intermediate recompression. [PDF p. 8, printed p. 958; anchor: normwise-error paragraph] [PDF p. 10, printed p. 960; anchor: transition to Lemma 3.4]
